entries.text: Ben drops a stone into a well. The stone falls a long way before it reaches the water.
A family takes food to the park. They sit under a tree and eat their meal outside.
We have picnics in the park.
We take a trip to a small town in spring.
我们春天去一个小镇旅行。
The bag looks heavy. In fact, it is very light.
这个包看起来很重。事实上，它很轻。
The library is near our home, so we go there on foot.
图书馆离家很近，所以我们步行去。
I get up ten minutes after I wake up.
I go to bed at ten, but I sometimes read before falling asleep.
我十点上床睡觉，但有时会先读会儿书再入睡。
Cooking and cleaning are part of our daily life.
做饭和清洁是我们日常生活的一部分。
I go to the office to pick up a letter waiting for me.
我去办公室取一封等我领取的信。
We clean up the playground after the sports day.
运动会后，我们把操场打扫干净。
Our drama club puts on a play each term.
我们的戏剧社团每学期上演一出戏。
The school puts on a concert for families.
学校为家长们举办音乐会。
We get the room ready for the class party.
我们把房间准备好，用来举办班级聚会。

Our class uses the school garden on Friday afternoon. Before we go outside, Mia goes to the office to pick up the key that our teacher left there. We open the garden gate and see cups and paper on the ground. Everyone helps to clean up the garden before the younger children arrive. Ben puts the cups in a box, and I put the paper in a bin. Soon the garden is clean again, and we can all enjoy reading outside together.

Our class wants to put on a short play for the other pupils. We choose a story about two friends who help each other. On Thursday, we get the hall ready for the show by moving the chairs into rows. Mia checks the pictures, while Ben makes sure that everyone can hear the music. I stand by the door and show the younger pupils where to sit. Everyone helps with a job, so we feel happy when the show begins.
Grandma knows the little shops near her home. She walks along a few short streets to buy food, while the nearest city is an hour away.
People often mention the old red bridge when they describe this place. Visitors take photos of it because its shape is different from the bridges nearby.
The children play on a sandy beach.
孩子们在铺满沙子的海滩上玩耍。
Mia kicks the ball to her brother.
米娅把球踢给她的哥哥／弟弟。
My grandparents live in a small town.
我的祖父母住在一个小镇。
The old bridge is a feature of our town.
这座老桥是我们镇的一个特色。
Our school is in the south of the town.
我们的学校在镇的南部。
Do you mind if I sit here?
This box is just the right size for my books.
这个箱子的大小恰好适合放我的书。
Clubs help students develop new interests.
社团帮助学生培养新的兴趣。
My reading skills develop as I read more.
随着阅读量增加，我的阅读技能不断发展。
Working together helps us solve the maths problem.
合作帮助我们解答数学题。
We look forward to meeting the new class teacher.
我们期待见到新的班主任。
Many students take part in the school sports day.
许多学生参加学校运动会。
练习帮助我们取得成功。
The class show is a great success.
We celebrate Grandma's birthday with a family dinner.
我们用家庭聚餐庆祝奶奶的生日。

Our school sports afternoon is next Wednesday, and Kai is excited about it. He tells his friend, “I look forward to running with our team.” His friend Lily wants to take part in the race too, although she does not run very fast. They meet after school to practise, and Kai waits when Lily needs a rest. Their teacher says that helping a teammate is as important as finishing the race. Now both friends feel ready to enjoy the afternoon together, whatever place they finish in.

The reading club plans a book sale to help buy books for younger pupils. At first, only a few people stop at the table, so the club puts up a big sign. Soon more families come, and all the books find new readers by the afternoon. The sale is a success because the club can buy the books it planned to buy. The members celebrate by sharing fruit and thanking everyone who helped. They are pleased because their work helps other children enjoy reading.
During a storm, a bright white flash crosses the sky. Mia sees it before she hears the loud sound.
Dad picks some beans from the garden this morning. He cooks them for lunch only an hour after picking them.
Please do not talk loudly in the library.
请不要在图书馆里大声说话。
We hear thunder on a rainy night.
我们在一个雨夜听到雷声。
We see lightning in the dark sky.
我们看见暗空中的闪电。
Dad buys fresh fruit every morning.
爸爸每天早上买新鲜水果。
We gather apples on the farm.
The garden is peaceful in the morning.
I wake up at seven in the morning.
Leo is willing to carry the books for us.
When I cannot solve a problem, I turn to my teacher for help.
解决不了问题时，我向老师求助。
I practise the guitar for fifteen minutes every day.
我每天练习吉他十五分钟。
The children are full of energy after a good rest.
好好休息后，孩子们充满活力。
I make new friends when I start junior high school.
进入初中时，我交到了新朋友。
We do the dishes together after dinner.

Lena wants to play the guitar at the class music afternoon. She decides to practise the same short song for ten minutes after school each day. Her friend Sam listens carefully and helps her with the difficult notes. They do not play all evening, because they also need time for homework and rest. On the day of the music afternoon, Lena feels full of energy and ready to play. She thanks Sam and enjoys sharing the song with the class.

This month, Tao starts junior high school and studies new subjects with new classmates. At first, he worries that his schoolwork will leave no time to help at home. His father suggests making a small plan instead of trying to do everything at once. Now Tao starts his homework after a short rest and helps to do the dishes after dinner. He puts the clean plates on the shelf, then gets his bag ready for the next morning. The plan gives him time for both school life and family jobs.
Rita points to the west side of a city map. This area has old homes, while other areas have new buildings.
Mia reads a magazine. One piece of writing explains how birds find food, and it fills two pages.
There is a snake under the tree.
The baby sleeps through the night.
This part of the town has many trees.
镇上的这个区域有很多树。
I read an article about birds.
我读一篇关于鸟的文章。
What is your reason for this answer?
你给出这个答案的理由是什么？
The park is alive with music.
公园里乐声四起，充满活力。
We are in the same class.
Can you describe your new classroom to me?
你能向我描述你的新教室吗？
Reading every day can improve your English.
每天阅读能改善你的英语水平。
We wait until a bus comes along.
我们等到一辆公共汽车出现。
Ben is good at drawing animals.
The story has a happy end: the two friends meet again.
故事有个圆满的结局：两个朋友再次相见。
Warm air rises above the heater.
暖空气上升到取暖器上方。
I am glad to see my old friend again.
再次见到老朋友，我很高兴。

Nina and Omar are writing a story together for the class reading corner. Nina is good at describing places, so she writes about the garden where the story begins. Omar enjoys writing what people say, and he adds a conversation between the two friends. At first, the story has a sad end: one friend leaves without saying anything. After reading it aloud, they change the final scene so that the friends explain their feelings. Both writers think this ending makes their story clearer and more complete.

Our class makes paper birds for a small school science activity. We take them outside on a windy afternoon and hold the strings carefully. When a stronger wind comes, some paper birds rise above our heads. Mine falls at first, so I change the fold and try again with a classmate. We are glad when it stays up for a few seconds instead of dropping at once. We compare our birds and talk about what helped them stay in the air.
The teacher has twelve cards. She puts four cards in each of three groups for the teams.
The club has three possible names. After discussing them, the members choose one name together.
The children make a sandcastle on the beach.
孩子们在海滩上堆沙堡。
The weather here follows the same pattern each year.
这里的天气每年都按同样的模式变化。
We divide the class into two groups.
We decide on a name for our club.
Rice is an important crop here.
水稻是这里的重要作物。
We learn about Chinese culture at school.
我们在学校学习中国文化。
The balloon rises into the sky.
Grandma watches over the little children in the garden.
奶奶在花园里照看小孩子。
A teacher watches over the group during the experiment.
一位老师在实验过程中监督小组。
The club teaches modern dance on Fridays.
My cousin is of medium height.
When I am absent, Mia takes my place in the school team.
我缺席时，米娅替代我参加校队。
People come and go at the busy station.
繁忙的车站里，人们来来去去。
The tired baby girl sometimes cries herself to sleep.
那个疲倦的女宝宝有时哭着入睡。
The fans cry out when their team scores.
球队得分时，球迷们大声叫喊。

Ella usually helps at the school library on Friday afternoon. This week she has to visit her grandmother, so Max offers to take Ella’s place for one afternoon. Ella shows him how to check the books and where to put the returned ones. Pupils come and go as they return old books and choose new ones. Max writes down the questions he cannot answer so that he can ask the librarian later. Ella thanks him, and the library can keep its usual opening time.

When Mei first stays at her aunt’s house, she misses her family very much. On the first night, she cries herself to sleep after saying goodnight to her parents by phone. The next morning, her aunt listens to her and helps her plan a call home each evening. Later, Mei sees her younger cousin nearly step on a toy and cries out, “Look down!” Her cousin stops safely, and they put the toys back in the box together. Mei still misses home, but the small plan and the time with her cousin make the visit easier.
Ben stops at a large sheet on the school wall. From its picture and words, he learns the time and place of the class show.
The pupils start a study about how beans grow. They watch the plants for two weeks and keep notes for their work.
Luckily, we get home before the storm begins.
幸好，我们在暴风雨开始前到家了。
I realize that I have the wrong timetable.
我意识到自己拿错了课程表。
We put a colourful poster about the concert on the wall.
我们在墙上贴了一张彩色音乐会海报。
Our science project is about how plants grow.
我们的科学课题是研究植物如何生长。
I write about my school day in my diary.
我在日记中记录校园生活。
I sincerely thank you for your patient help.
我真诚地感谢你耐心的帮助。
The students act in a short drama about friendship.
学生们演出一部关于友谊的短剧。
A good night's sleep gives me energy for the next day.
睡个好觉能让我第二天精力充沛。
My brother is in Grade Seven.
A friendly greeting can make a new student feel welcome.
友好的问候能让新同学感到受欢迎。
My fourteen-year-old cousin is a teenager.
我十四岁的表亲是青少年。
This magazine has a new issue every month.
这本杂志每月出版一期。
The magazine has a section for teen readers.
这本杂志有面向青少年读者的栏目。
Making a clear poster is a useful skill.
制作清晰的海报是一项实用技能。
Our school has a reading club that meets every Tuesday.
我们学校有一个每周二活动的阅读社团。
Making a class poster is a fun group activity.
制作班级海报是一项有趣的小组活动。
The team has a rocky start, but the players learn to work together.
球队开局艰难，但队员们逐渐学会合作。
We pack our clothes into a small case for the trip.
我们把旅行衣服装进一个小箱子。
A friendly message can put me in a good mood.
一条友好的消息能让我心情愉快。
Our group gives a presentation to show how the model works.
我们小组做演示，展示模型怎样运行。

Our class plans to visit a small science room at another school. The planning has a rocky start because the bus time changes and two helpers become ill. Instead of cancelling the visit, we ask our teacher to help make a new timetable. On the morning of the visit, we pack our notebooks and bottles of water in our bags. We meet ten minutes earlier than before, so everyone has time to check what they need. The visit goes ahead, and we learn that a careful new plan can help when things are difficult.

Tina has to give a short talk about her favourite book in front of the class. Before lunch, her mood is low because she worries that she may forget what to say. Her partner helps her choose three small pictures to remind her of the main points. They practise once, and Tina notices that she can speak without reading every word. During her presentation, she holds up the pictures and explains why the story matters to her. Afterwards, she feels pleased because she shared her ideas in her own words.
Lily draws a line with a ruler. The line goes in one direction and has no bends.
Ben describes his new classmate. He talks about her hair, eyes and height, not her hobbies.
We learn some basic words before we read the story.
读故事之前，我们先学一些基础词汇。
He has dark hair and brown eyes.
他头发乌黑，眼睛是褐色的。
Her hair is long and straight.
The picture helps us talk about the man's appearance.
这张图片帮助我们谈论那位男士的外貌。
A caring friend notices when you need help.
体贴的朋友会留意到你何时需要帮助。
Being patient is an important quality in a good teacher.
有耐心是好老师的一项重要品质。
Honesty is one of the personal qualities I look for in a friend.
诚实是我选择朋友时看重的一种个性品质。
Our class does a survey about favourite school subjects.
我们班就最喜欢的学科做调查。
There is trust between us because we keep our promises.
我们信守承诺，所以彼此信任。
Our friendship grows as we help each other.
我们在互相帮助中增进友谊。
It takes courage to tell the truth about your own mistake.
说出自己的错误需要勇气。
After a week of practice, Leo feels confident about his talk.
经过一周练习，利奥对自己的演讲充满信心。
Our teacher is patient when we ask the same question again.
我们再次问同一个问题时，老师很有耐心。
Ella is honest: she tells the teacher about her mistake.
埃拉很诚实：她把自己的错误告诉老师。
Sam plays the guitar in the school music club.
萨姆在学校音乐社团弹吉他。
There is a small bookshelf in the corner of our classroom.
教室角落里有一个小书架。
In geography, we learn about rivers and mountains.
地理课上，我们学习河流与山脉。
My heart beats faster after running.
跑步后，我的心跳得更快。
She has a kind heart and likes helping others.
她心地善良，喜欢帮助别人。
A kind thought can lead to a helpful action.
一个善意的想法可以带来一次助人行动。

Our class makes a small map of the school for new pupils. Mia puts the library in one corner of the paper, where two edges meet. In geography, we learn how maps help people understand places. We add the playground, the gate and the paths between them. Ben checks the map by walking from the gate to the library. He finds one missing path, so we draw it before making copies. Now visitors can use our map to find the places they need.

Grandpa enjoys sitting outside, but the old garden seat is broken. Mia has a thought: the family can help him find a comfortable chair. She tells her brother, and they ask their parents about a spare chair. Their father says Mia has a kind heart because she notices what Grandpa needs. The children clean the spare chair while their father checks that it is strong. They place it beside the flowers where Grandpa likes to sit. Grandpa smiles, and the family spends a quiet afternoon there together.
The music starts before lunch. It does not stop during lunch and is still playing afterwards.
Mr Green grows rice on his farm. He digs the ground and plants the young rice plants every spring.
We buy vegetables from a local farmer.
我们从一位当地农民那里买蔬菜。
Eating together at the festival is a family tradition.
节日里一起吃饭是这个家庭的传统。
The rain may continue all afternoon.
这场雨可能会持续整个下午。
Farmers work their land to grow food.
农民耕种土地来种植粮食。
Qingming is a solar term in the traditional Chinese calendar.
清明是中国传统历法中的一个节气。
Our class is divided into four groups for the activity.
我们的班级为这项活动被分成四组。

Every autumn, our family likes to take a trip to Aunt May's farm. We travel by train and carry our lunch in a blue bag. Aunt May meets us and shows us the fruit trees beside her house. We often have picnics on the grass there instead of eating inside. My brother spreads a cloth, and I put out the bread and apples. After lunch, we put every cup and bag away before helping Aunt May. The visit gives us time together and a change from our busy town life.

Our class visits the park after a night of rain. The grass is wet, and small drops of water shine on every leaf. Near the bridge, the water is deep, so our teacher chooses a path away from it. We stay on the path and watch the ducks from a wooden bench. Lily draws the birds while Ben counts the different colours he can see. Nobody needs to step on the grass to finish the activity. Back at school, we put our drawings together to show the park after rain.
Bees help many plants grow. They play an important part in life on Earth.
The school uses cards, shelves and a computer together to lend books. Each part connects with the others so pupils can find and return books.
The teacher keeps one folder for each pupil. A folder holds all the information about that pupil in one place.
This story is based on a real family.
这个故事以一个真实家庭为基础。
Trees play an important part in keeping the air clean.
树木在保持空气清洁方面发挥重要作用。
The school has a system for sharing books.
学校有一套共享图书的系统。
The school keeps a file for each student.
学校为每个学生保存一份档案。
这只蝴蝶的色彩令人惊叹。
Earth is the planet where we live.
地球是我们居住的行星。

In our small town, children play football in the square after school. There are houses and shops nearby, so everyone keeps the ball away from the windows. Ben likes to kick the ball to a teammate instead of sending it towards a shop. A younger child wants to join, but she has no team yet. The older pupils invite her and make the teams the same size. She soon learns where to stand and who can help her. The square becomes a place where children of different ages play together.

Sara and her father visit a sandy beach early in the morning. They leave the busy road and hear only waves and a few birds. The beach is peaceful before the crowds arrive. Sara sits on a dry rock and draws the lines that the water makes on the sand. Her father writes a few words about the sounds in a small notebook. They compare their notes and pictures before walking back to the bus stop. Both find that a quiet visit helps them notice things they usually miss.
Mia draws a line around three villages and their fields on a map. She colours this part of the country green for her report.
Ben waits for a bus in thick gloves and still feels painfully cold. Ice covers the ground, and he wishes he could go indoors.
One billion is one thousand million.
Snow covers the ground in winter.
Many families live in this area.
许多家庭住在这个地区。
It is freezing outside, so I wear a warm coat.
外面极冷，所以我穿一件暖和的外套。
Our school is in the north of the town.
我们的学校在镇的北部。
The North Pole is very cold.

Ben and Lily see a small dog alone near the park gate. Lily calls loudly so the people across the path can hear her. Nobody answers, and Ben notices a name card on the dog's collar. The card is covered with mud, which is the reason they cannot read the phone number. They ask a park worker for help instead of leaving the dog alone. The worker cleans the card and calls the owner, who comes to the gate. The children are glad that asking for help brings the dog and its owner together.

Our reading club meets in a quiet part of the town near the library. One Saturday, rain falls through the whole morning, from the time we arrive until lunch. We cannot sit outside, so the librarian opens a room with a large table. Each person brings a different book and reads a favourite page to the group. Mia writes the book titles on the board so we can find them later. At lunch, our parents arrive with umbrellas to take us home. The rainy morning gives us new books to share instead of stopping our meeting.
The shelf is low. Lily stretches out her arm and can touch the book without a chair.
Mia opens a bag of rice. One tiny seed falls onto the table, and she puts it back in the bag.
Few plants grow in this dry desert.
很少有植物生长在这片干旱的沙漠里。
The door is about two metres high.
I can reach the low shelf without a chair.
不用椅子我也够得着这个低书架。
There is a grain of rice on the table.
A whale comes to the surface to breathe.

In a storybook, a village holds the same three festivals every year. The events follow a clear pattern: people gather, share songs and end with a meal. A new family wants to learn about the village's culture. The neighbours invite them to help put tables in the square. While working together, they hear old stories and ask about the festival food. The children learn a song and join the other children at the meal. By taking part, the family learns more than it can learn from pictures alone.

The science club has a garden beside the school kitchen. At the start of the term, the pupils divide it into two growing areas. They choose beans as one crop and plant rice in the other area. Each group makes a label so visitors know what grows there. Mia records the plant heights, and Ben checks the water each morning. They compare their notes to see how the two growing areas change. The club plans to show these notes beside the plants on the school open day.
Lena feels worried about her school project. Her friends listen to her ideas and help her keep trying.
A group enters a garden for the first time. They walk along different paths to find out what is growing there.
A butterfly rests on the yellow flower.
一只蝴蝶停在黄色的花朵上。
The school provides clean drinking water for students.
学校为学生提供洁净的饮用水。
My friends support me when I feel worried.
当我感到担忧时，我的朋友支持我。
Light and water support the growth of plants.
光和水维持植物的生长。
We explore the island and draw a map of it.
我们探索这座岛并画出它的地图。
The sun disappears behind a cloud.
This ruler is made of plastic.
这把尺子是塑料制成的。

Our family visits Grandfather's farm at the beginning of spring. He works his land each year to grow vegetables for the nearby town. On the first planting day, every family member helps with one row. Grandfather says this is a family tradition that his parents taught him. My aunt shows me how to leave enough space between the young plants. After our work, we sit together and listen to stories about earlier planting days. I understand that growing food also gives our family a way to share time and stories.

A free reading club opens in the room beside our town library. The local people bring books and offer to read with younger children. These volunteers play an important part in keeping the club open every weekend. One person welcomes new readers while another helps them choose a book. The children can ask questions and try reading a page aloud without feeling rushed. At the end, everyone helps return the books to their shelves. Because people share the jobs, the club becomes a friendly place for the whole town.
In winter, snow covers the fields.
Ben makes a poster about a very large number. He writes 1,000,000,000, then checks that there is one followed by nine zeros.
At a sea-life display, Mia sees a picture of a huge animal. The animal lives in the sea but comes to the surface to breathe air.

Our class builds a model of Earth for a map activity. A thin line goes through the ball, and its top end has a North Pole label. We make a system of numbered cards and matching labels to organise the activity. Each card gives a place name and asks a pupil to find it on the model. Ben checks that every card number has the right label before the game starts. Mia holds the model while younger pupils take turns choosing their cards. The cards help us share the model without everyone reaching for it at once.

In winter, my family visits Grandma in the north of our country. It is freezing on the morning we arrive, and even the puddles have ice. Grandma waits inside her warm house and waves from the window. Before going into the garden, we put on thick coats and gloves. We check the empty bird feeder and add some food from Grandma's cupboard. Then we return inside and watch from the window while sharing a hot meal. The visit is a chance to help Grandma and enjoy being together, even on a cold day.
Lily walks in the rain without an umbrella. Water soaks her coat and runs from her sleeves when she goes inside.
Ben walks across soft mud. After he lifts his foot, a clear mark of the bottom of his shoe stays behind.

Our art club wants to draw something different from the school buildings. We decide to take a trip to a lake with our teacher. Everyone packs a notebook, pencils and a simple lunch for the day. We often have picnics during club visits, and this time we choose a table under a tree. After eating, each person chooses one view and draws it for twenty minutes. Before leaving, we compare the pictures and notice that no two are exactly the same. The same lake gives everyone a different idea to bring back to school.

Our class chooses a clear morning for a walk to the park. There is not a cloud in the sky, and everyone can see the map easily. The park is in the south of our town, below the school on our map with north at the top. Mia holds the map while Ben checks the street names at each corner. At one corner, the street sign is hidden behind leaves, so we stop and look again. We find the sign and continue together until the park gate comes into view. By using both the map and the signs, we arrive without taking the wrong road.
The cleaner has a bottle of a strong substance used to clean windows. Its label says to keep the contents away from food.
The villagers pump drinking water from a deep well. The water is below the soil before it comes through the pipe.
We protect the trees by keeping fires away from them.
我们让火远离树木，以保护树木。
Some cleaning chemicals are harmful if people drink them.
有些清洁化学品如果被人饮用会有害。
Some villages use groundwater for drinking.
有些村庄使用地下水饮用。
干燥的木头很容易燃烧。
A small fire burns the dry leaves.
Workers take oil from deep below the ground.
工人从地下深处开采石油。

Our school hall is usually quiet before lessons begin. On the day of the clubs fair, it is alive with music and excited voices. Mia visits the tables and asks pupils why they enjoy their clubs. She writes an article for the school magazine about what she sees and hears. Instead of naming only the biggest club, she includes small groups with interesting ideas. Her teacher checks the names before the magazine goes to print. The article helps readers discover activities they might otherwise miss.

Our class visits a nature centre to draw different animals. A long green snake rests behind a glass window in one room. Ben speaks loudly at first, and the pupils nearby cannot hear the guide. The guide points to a quiet sign and asks everyone to listen. Ben lowers his voice, and Mia asks how to draw the animal's long shape. The guide shows them a picture, and they work in their notebooks beside the window. Their drawings improve because everyone has space and can hear the instructions.
Lia opens the school page in her internet browser. She can click different pages there to read news and find club information.
Mia does not borrow this bike from anyone. It belongs to her, and she keeps it at home.
Some families use natural gas to cook meals.
有些家庭使用天然气做饭。
Dirty water can be harmful to animals.
Our school website has news about the sports day.
我们学校的网站上有关于运动会的新闻。
I have my own desk in my room.
我的房间里有我自己的书桌。
The walk is long. However, the view is wonderful.
路程很长。然而，景色很美。
The emperor in this story lives in a large palace.
这个故事里的皇帝住在一座大宫殿里。

At our town museum, a volunteer shows us a model of an old ship engine. Beside it is a sealed bottle of oil, the dark liquid from underground used as fuel. A clear cover helps protect the model from dust and visitors' hands. We look closely without moving the cover or opening the bottle. Ben draws the engine, and Mia copies the information from its label. They put their work together to make a page for our class display. The small exhibit gives us a way to learn from old objects while keeping them in good condition.

Our class visits a small farm to learn how its greenhouse works. A tank holds groundwater that the farmer pumps from a well below the field. The farmer uses this water for the young plants growing inside. On cold mornings, dry wood can burn in a closed stove to give the room heat. We watch from the doorway while the farmer explains the water tank and stove. One group draws the water supply, and another draws the heating equipment. Back at school, we combine the drawings to explain what we learned during the visit.
The two countries want peace, so they agree to end the war.
Strong wind carries so much dry sand across the road that the sky turns brown. The driver stops because he cannot see the road ahead.
The pupils cannot hear the recording at the back of the room. They move the speaker to the centre, and now everyone can hear it clearly.
Some birds hunt small animals for food.
有些鸟捕猎小动物作为食物。
The people hope the war will end soon.
人们希望战争很快结束。
People stay indoors during the sandstorm.
沙暴期间人们待在室内。
Working together helps us find a solution.
共同努力帮助我们找到解决办法。
A cold wind blows across the field.
Ben blows on the hot soup before tasting it.
本品尝热汤前先朝它吹气。
My grandparents and I belong to different generations.
我和祖父母属于不同的世代。

Our class rehearses a play about an emperor who rules an imaginary country. Sam wants to wear the paper crown and give all the orders. However, his character must first listen to a gardener with a better plan. The gardener explains how a dry garden can receive water from a nearby stream. When Sam speaks more calmly, the scene becomes easier for everyone to follow. We keep this version because the ruler learns to value another person's ideas.

The reading club wants a place to share short reviews of favourite books. Lena builds a simple website with three pages: books, reviews and questions. At first, she copies a sentence from a book because she cannot think of an opening. Her partner asks what she herself likes about the story. Lena writes her own review about the brave girl and the surprising ending. They test every page on the classroom computer before showing it to the club. Lena is pleased that visitors can read ideas that truly belong to her.
Our fact file about pandas lists their food, homes and size.
After the wind, leaves lie across every part of the shed roof. From below, Mia cannot see any of the roof tiles.
The team checks the two open rooms for a lost box. Mia says it is not in those rooms, but it might still be in the locked room they cannot check.
The Earth is one of the planets in the solar system.
地球是太阳系中的一颗行星。
I make a fact file about pandas for our class project.
我为班级项目制作了一份关于熊猫的事实档案。
The ground is covered by snow in this picture.
这张图中的地面被积雪覆盖。
As far as we know, the library opens at nine.
据我们所知，图书馆九点开门。
This town is ten metres above sea level.
这个镇位于海平面以上十米处。
The park is near our school. What's more, it is free to visit.
公园离学校很近。更重要的是，参观免费。

Grandma brings an old kite to our family picnic beside the lake. Her father showed her how to make it when she was a child. Now three generations—Grandma, Dad and me—repair its loose string together. The wind starts to blow, but the kite turns in circles near the ground. Dad holds it while Grandma checks the string, and I change the paper tail. On the next try, it rises above us, and we cheer together. I draw our family and the kite in my diary that evening.

During a visit to a desert town, our class stays inside the visitor centre. Outside, a sandstorm fills the air with dry sand, and we cannot see the bus clearly. For the next hour, nobody can take the planned outdoor walk. The guide asks for a solution to the problem of a bored class. We use our notebooks to make a picture story about the places we saw earlier. By the time the air is clear again, everyone has a page to share.
Mia takes care of her little brother when their parents are busy.
After lunch by the river, the pupils see bags, bottle caps and wrappers caught between the stones. These man-made plastic items are dirtying the shore instead of being put in bins.
A dead tree is leaning towards a path. Workers use a saw at its base and bring the whole tree to the ground.
The school provides children with healthy lunches.
学校为孩子们提供健康午餐。
Ben takes care of his little sister after school.
本放学后照顾他的妹妹。
Using fewer plastic bags can help reduce plastic pollution.
少用塑料袋有助于减少塑料污染。
Please do not cut down the old tree.
Hundreds of people visit the park each day.
每天都有数以百计的人参观这个公园。
A strong wind can blow away dry leaves.

Our class makes a model island for an open afternoon at school. A blue line around its base marks sea level, and tiny hills rise above it. We want visitors to understand the model without asking us to explain every part. Mia writes short labels beside the hills and the small harbour. “What's more, we can add a key to explain the colours,” Ben suggests. We put the key near the front and ask another pupil to test it. She finds the harbour at once, so we know our display is easier to read.

Our class is making a small map of the school garden. In an old photo, the stone path is easy to see. Today it is covered by fallen leaves, so we follow its edge rather than stepping into the flower beds. “As far as we know, the path ends at the old gate,” Mia says. Before drawing the final line, we ask the gardener to check our guess. He shows us a short turn behind a bush that is missing from the photo. We change the map and add the date beside the new line.
These families need milk. Can this small farm provide families with fresh milk?
Ben opens a tiny paper box, and a large paper castle unfolds from it. Everyone stops talking and asks, “How did all that fit inside?”
The school keeps a club's paper reports, member list and old photographs in one labelled folder. When a new teacher needs its history, she opens the folder to read these organised records.

Several classes make a wall picture from hundreds of paper leaves for the open afternoon. Each pupil writes a kind message on a leaf before we sort them by colour. We first spread the leaves on tables beside an open window. A strong wind can blow away the light pieces, so Mia closes the window. Then we fix the leaves to a large tree shape on the wall. Visitors stop to read the messages, and we keep a photograph after the event.

Before our class picnic, the park keeper shows us a change near the lake. Workers must cut down a dead tree because a crack makes it unsafe. They leave the healthy trees standing and close only the small work area. Farther along the shore, we find plastic pollution: bags and bottles lie between the stones. We collect the rubbish with the keeper and sort it into the marked bins. At lunch, we discuss two jobs—caring for trees and keeping waste out of the park.
These two areas have different weather. One is wet and the other is dry.
Before the guessing game, Ben spreads a cloth over a model so nobody can see it. He removes the cloth when everyone is ready.
Ben writes the digit one and then nine zeros. He wants a single word for that very large number.

For a geography game, we turn a long table into an imaginary desert. Yellow paper covers the dry-looking land, with a few model plants beside a small water place. A ruler shows that the route across the table is one metre long. We place cards for water, food and a tent along the route. Each team moves a paper traveller and explains which card to visit next. The game lets us practise journey planning, while the ruler keeps every team's route the same length.

We use a plain ball to make a model of Earth. The teacher draws Earth's axis through the ball and marks a pole at each end. We draw land and sea, then add two direction cards. N stands for north, so we place that card by the top end. I first put both cards together, but Ben checks the labels with me. We move one card to the other end and test the model with another group.
The students collect water from the river in small bottles for their science lesson.
The final bell rings, and Mia walks through the school gate towards her home. A few minutes later, she is no longer on the school grounds.
Lena sees a route sign showing one thousand metres to the river. She wants to describe that distance using a larger unit.
An astronaut wears a spacesuit to work outside the spacecraft.
宇航员穿着航天服在航天器外工作。
We collect fallen leaves for our science lesson.
我们为科学课采集落叶。
We leave home at seven every morning.
我们每天早晨七点离开家。
The park is one kilometre from my house.
After being ill, Ben feels weak and needs to rest.
生病后，本觉得身体虚弱，需要休息。
Please tie the boat to the post with this rope.
请用这根绳子把船拴在柱子上。

For our history project, I interview Grandpa about his old kitchen. In a photo, a pipe supplies natural gas to the kitchen cooker. I ask if everyone in his generation cooked in the same way. He laughs and shows a neighbour's photo with a very different stove. We choose both photos instead of writing one simple rule about all older people. Before finishing, we add names and dates under the pictures. Our page shows that people of a similar age can still have different lives.

Aunt Lin hangs our homemade wind chime beside the balcony door. When the wind begins to blow, the short metal pieces touch and make soft sounds. However, a long ribbon wraps around them, and the sound stops. We need a solution that keeps the decoration but lets the pieces move freely. I fasten the ribbon to the top ring instead of leaving it between the pieces. The next breeze brings the sound back, and Aunt Lin asks me to explain the change. We draw the new arrangement so we can make another chime later.
After a short run, Mia stops in the shade. Her chest moves gently as she takes air in and lets it out again.
The school opens a new place for sport, with practice rooms, changing rooms and exercise equipment. Clubs can book it for their training.
低于通常（或平均）数量（或水平、价值）的
The shop sells good books at low prices.
这家商店以低价出售好书。
We breathe fresh air in the park.
我们在公园里呼吸新鲜空气。
Our school has new sports facilities.
我们学校有新的体育设施。
The children's night in the forest becomes an adventure.
孩子们在森林里度过的一夜变成了一次冒险经历。
沿某方向前进；向某方向移动
A boat passes under the bridge.

Our class makes welcome boxes for pupils returning after a long absence. I tie a blue string around one box so the lid stays in place. Inside are a card, a pencil and notes from different classmates. When Ben returns after being ill, he still feels weak and cannot carry many books. We put the box on his desk and ask which jobs he wants help with. He chooses a book-carrying partner but reads the messages by himself. The welcome is quiet, and Ben decides when to join the louder games.

The walking club meets at school beside a map of two routes to the river. One route is a kilometre long; the other is shorter but crosses a busy car park. Our teacher chooses the longer route because it follows a quiet path. Before we leave the school gate, everyone checks their water and meeting time. Along the path, we mark a small bridge and a noticeboard on our maps. At the river, each pair compares its map with another pair. We agree that a useful route description tells more than just the distance.
We need to prepare the room before the guests arrive.
Nina keeps drawings of spacecraft above her desk. She hopes to build a machine that can explore the Moon when she is older.
The music teacher invites Mia to play one piece at next week's show. This would be her first school performance.
We do an experiment to find out which material keeps water warm.
我们做一个实验，找出哪种材料能让水保持温热。
We prepare lunch before our guests arrive.
我们在客人到来之前准备午饭。
n. 梦想；理想；v. 做梦；梦见
My dream is to become a doctor.
我的梦想是成为一名医生。
I sometimes dream about flying when I am asleep.
我睡着时有时会梦见飞翔。
The school show gives us a chance to sing on stage.
学校演出给了我们登台演唱的机会。
I send a letter to my cousin.
Mia sends a message to her mother.
米娅给妈妈发了一条消息。
Read the introduction before the first chapter.
请在读第一章之前先读引言。

The museum guide gives our group a card with a drawing of a small key. We must follow three clues to find the room shown on the back. As we pass under a low arch, Mia notices the same key shape above a doorway. The next clue sends us to a room with a large model ship. We compare its flag with our card and discover the final sign. This small adventure makes us look carefully instead of hurrying past the displays. At the end, we return the card and explain which clue was hardest.

Our class visits a new sports facility beside the school field. It has an exercise room, changing rooms and a place to fill water bottles. Before trying anything, we walk around with the coach and read the simple instructions. After a short run, I stop in the rest area and breathe steadily. The coach asks us to notice the space around each piece of equipment. We draw a plan showing where people can move, rest and get water. Our plans help the next class find what it needs without crowding one doorway.
I hope to visit my friend in another country someday.
Liu spends a weekend helping on a farm. Back home, he describes feeding hens and gathering beans, telling his friends what the visit was like.
In a space story, a small machine travels from a larger space vehicle to the Moon. It settles on the surface and sends pictures back.
The window gives us a beautiful view of the river.
从这扇窗户能看到美丽的河景。
I hope to visit the moon someday.
我希望有朝一日能去月球。
Our first night in a tent is an exciting experience.
我们第一次在帐篷里过夜是一次令人兴奋的经历。
My grandmother has a lot of experience in growing vegetables.
我祖母在种菜方面有丰富的经验和阅历。
The lander carries tools to study the Moon.
着陆器携带工具研究月球。
We can see a small island in the lake.
我们能看见湖中有一座小岛。
We visit an ancient town with very old stone houses.
我们游览一座有很老的石屋的古镇。

Our class makes a small garden guide for next year's pupils. Before the maps and pictures, the introduction explains why we made it and how to use it. At first, the opening is so long that two readers stop before the first map. We shorten it to four clear sentences and add a question for the readers. Then we send a copy by email to a younger class and ask for comments. Their teacher replies that the shorter opening helps the children start exploring. We keep both versions to see how our writing improves.

Mia's dream is to design machines that can explore places people cannot easily reach. The science club offers a chance to speak with an engineer, so she writes her name down. She first plans ten questions, but the group has only fifteen minutes. Mia chooses one question about testing a small model before building a larger machine. The engineer asks about her idea and listens as she explains her drawing. Afterwards, Mia adds two notes to her design instead of throwing the first plan away. The meeting gives her a clearer next step, although more work remains.
Mia's model bridge falls during three tests. Each time, she checks the broken part, changes her plan and tries again instead of giving up.
Mia studies a picture of our solar system, then a wider picture with distant groups of stars. She asks for the name that includes all space and everything in it, not just one system.
Mia writes a short poem about the rain.
米娅写了一首关于雨的短诗。
Music helps us express our feelings.
音乐帮助我们表达感受。
She shows determination and keeps trying after each mistake.
她表现出坚毅，在每次出错后继续尝试。
The universe contains all the stars and planets.
宇宙包含所有恒星和行星。
It is only seven, but Lily is already at school.
才七点，但莉莉已经在学校了。
A century is one hundred years.

Our history club takes a small boat to an island in the lake. We follow the guide to an ancient stone wall above the shore. The stones are uneven, and a picture shows how the old building once looked. Instead of guessing every missing part, we mark the parts we can still see. Mia draws the doorway, while I compare its shape with the picture. On the boat home, we put our sketches beside the guide's notes. Our final page separates what we observed from what the picture suggests.

Our club builds a model lander to carry a paper flag onto a sand tray. We lower it from a chair instead of throwing it. On the first test, the flag falls out when the model touches the sand. Mia adds a paper holder, and we repeat the test in the same way. Now the flag stays inside until we open the model. The experience shows us why one change is easier to judge than many at once. We record both results before planning another test.
Our class reads two poems about the Moon. Each has four short lines.
After a picnic, many plastic bags and bottles are left on the beach. The rubbish makes the beach dirty and harms the animals there.
A neighbour is away for a week. Dan feeds her cat each day, fills its water bowl and makes sure it is safe.

At the back of our family shop stands a small wooden cupboard. A label says that it was made more than a century ago. Grandfather already cleaned it, but one of its doors is still stuck. He asks me to hold a lamp while he checks the lock. Inside, we find old photographs and a notebook full of family names. We do not throw anything away because the objects tell our family story. By evening, the cupboard is open and everyone has something new to ask.

Ravi borrows a book about the universe from the small village library. He wants to tell his younger sister about the stars in its pictures. At first, several pages are too difficult for him to understand. Instead of returning the book, he writes questions and visits the librarian. His determination helps him keep learning a little after school each day. A week later, he can explain one picture in his own words. His sister listens carefully, then asks to borrow the book with him.
Before interviewing the gardener, we will prepare five questions about growing vegetables.
Ling puts equal pieces of ice in two cups and places the cups in different parts of the room. She records how quickly each piece melts to check an idea.
In a story, a guide shows visitors a stone bowl made by people thousands of years ago. Nobody uses it for meals now; it is kept in a museum.

Zoe has only a little pocket money, but she wants a book about cooking. At a second-hand book stall, she finds one with a torn cover. Its price is low, so she can buy it without using all her money. Before paying, she reads the introduction at the front. It explains that the recipes use simple tools found in most kitchens. Zoe checks the pages and sees that none are missing. She takes the book home and chooses a recipe to try with Dad.

One rainy afternoon, Ana finds a postcard from her cousin in another town. The picture shows a bridge that is new to Ana. She decides to send a card back instead of writing only a short message. She draws the pond near her home and adds three sentences about it. The cards give both cousins a chance to learn about each other's neighbourhood. When the next card arrives, Ana marks the new place on a small map. Soon their map has pictures from both towns.
Nora slides her hand across the top of a desk. She feels some rough parts and wants to make that outer layer smooth.
Kai holds a paper plane gently between his fingers. He then opens his fingers and lets the plane move freely into the air.
Our neighbour lives in the house next to ours.
我们的邻居住在我们隔壁的房子里。
A leaf floats on the surface of the water.
放开；松开；使自由移动（或飞翔、降落等）
We open our hands and release the butterfly.
This bag of rice weighs one kilogram.
Our school has a programme to help students read more.
我们学校有一项帮助学生多阅读的计划。

Every month, Aunt Lin lets local musicians put on a free concert in her café. One Saturday, heavy rain brings mud through the open door just before the music starts. The musicians keep their instruments dry while people from next door clean up the floor. I bring old towels, and my brother moves the wet chairs away. Soon there is a dry space for everyone to sit. When the first song begins, the audience is smaller than usual but very cheerful. Aunt Lin thanks the helpers with warm drinks after the last song.

On Sunday, my sister and I visit our neighbour for her birthday. We get a bag ready for the visit by putting a card and some fruit inside. Dad plans to drive us, but the car will not start. The neighbour's house is only three streets away, so we decide to go on foot. We follow a quiet path and stop to look at the flowers. When we arrive, our neighbour invites us to share the fruit. The short journey becomes part of her birthday story.
We do exercise every morning to keep our bodies strong and healthy.
Ari lifts a camera and points it towards a bright flower. He presses a button, and a picture of the flower is saved.
In a space story, a craft rises from the Earth. It reaches a path where it goes around the planet again and again instead of returning to the ground.
Astronauts live and work on a space station.
航天员在空间站上生活和工作。
We do exercise in the park to keep healthy.
我们在公园锻炼以保持健康。
We take photos of the flowers with a camera.
我们用相机给花朵拍照。
A rocket helps the satellite get into orbit around Earth.
火箭帮助卫星进入绕地球的轨道。
Thousands of people visit the island in summer.
夏天，数以千计的人来这座岛游览。
This guide gives us information about the island.
这本指南向我们提供关于这座岛的信息。

Our community centre starts a cooking programme for families on Saturday mornings. In the first lesson, each group receives one kilogram of flour for two small recipes. The leader asks us to read both recipes before we begin. Some of the flour is for bread, and the rest is for simple biscuits. My father measures the first part while I write labels for the bowls. We keep the bowls separate so that we do not use all the flour in one recipe. At the end, every family takes home something made together.

Grandfather and I make a small boat from a piece of light wood. We carry it to a shallow pond where the surface is smooth and still. I hold the boat near the edge while Grandfather checks its little sail. When he is ready, I release the boat and move my hands away. A gentle wind carries it slowly towards the other side. We walk along the bank and watch without touching it. Grandfather lifts it out with a long stick, and we plan a second journey.
The Sun sets in the west.
Mira opens a box for her craft work. Wooden beads and glass beads are together inside, and she decides to use both kinds in one necklace.
A club in China plans an evening about France and Canada. The members choose pictures and stories from both countries for their display.
The village is in the east of the country.
这个村庄在国家的东部。
We walk east towards the rising Sun.
我们向东走，朝着太阳升起的方向。
Their house is in the west of the town.
他们的房子在镇的西部。
We walk west as the Sun goes down.
太阳落下时，我们向西走。
The music is a mix of old and new styles.
这种音乐是旧风格与新风格的结合。
This restaurant serves western food such as pizza.
这家餐厅供应比萨饼等西方食物。
The artist has a simple style of painting.
这位画家的绘画风格简洁。
大众喜爱的；广受欢迎的
This song is popular with students.

Our town cinema shows a film about a young space team. Before the show, thousands of fans wait outside, filling the square and nearby streets. The film follows a team that builds a spacecraft after several failed tests. During the final scene, the craft leaves the ground and gets into orbit. It travels around the Earth again and again along its new path. The team members smile because their long months of work lead to a good result. Walking home, I talk about the team's patience rather than the bright special effects.

On Saturday, our street club gives families a small challenge. We must find three interesting shapes during a walk and take photos of them. My mother is pleased because she wants to do exercise without going to a sports centre. We notice a round window, a star on a gate and a triangle painted on a wall. Instead of rushing, we stop safely beside each place and look closely. Back at home, we put the pictures on one page and mark our walking route. The challenge helps us see familiar streets in a new way.
Maya is twenty-five years old and teaches at a school. She makes her own plans and lives in her own flat.
Mr Hua is seventy-five and no longer works full-time. He enjoys visiting the community centre with other people of his age.
This is the site of the new school.
这是新学校的建校地点。
The bank is across the street from the school.
Children need an adult with them on this trip.
这次旅行中，孩子们需要有一名成年人陪同。
The centre has activities for seniors.
这个中心有供老年人参加的活动。
The customer buys a bag of rice.
The design shows the places for the windows.
这份设计展示窗户的位置。

Nia wants a different style for her old jacket, but she cannot buy a new one. The jacket still fits well, so Mum suggests changing only a few small parts. They replace the plain buttons with blue ones and add a white stripe. Nia wears it to school and tells her friends how they changed it. Two friends ask if she can help them plan similar changes. The simple look becomes popular with her friends, although the jacket is not new. Nia keeps a drawing of the jacket to plan another change later.

Our music club is preparing a short show for families. We want the music to include something for every visitor. Lea chooses a Chinese song, while Tom finds a Western song in a British music book. The final mix gives the show two different sounds without making it too long. Both songs have an easy part that the audience can repeat. We write the words on large cards and practise the change between the songs. At the show, even people who do not know the songs join in at that part.
Leo often forgets which page he read last. A friend suggests putting a paper strip between the pages before closing the book.
In a space story, a team makes the first successful journey to a new world. People say the event will be remembered in history books for years.
What else do we need for the picnic?
野餐我们还需要别的什么？
My suggestion is to visit the library after lunch.
我的建议是午饭后去图书馆。
The teacher gives us a useful tip for spelling.
老师给我们一条实用的拼写提示。
历史上著名（或重要）的；可名垂青史的
The museum stands near a historic building important to the town.
博物馆位于一座对这个镇有历史意义的建筑附近。
Write the students' names on this list.
把学生们的名字写在这份名单上。
The landscape has hills, fields and a river.
这片风景中有山丘、田野和一条河流。

At a small bakery, a customer finds that her biscuits are broken when she gets home. The owner asks our class for a new design for the box. We look at the old box and notice large empty spaces inside. Anya folds thick paper into small parts to keep each biscuit in its own space. Our group tests the box by carrying it around the playground. The biscuits stay whole, so the owner tries our idea in the shop. She also thanks the buyer for telling her about the problem.

At the library, people of different ages meet to make a booklet of poems. One senior, Mrs Hua, brings a poem she remembers from childhood. Chen, an adult, volunteers to help arrange the page. Mrs Hua explains why she chose the poem, and Chen writes her words beside it. They check the page together before adding it to the booklet. A child reads their page and asks Mrs Hua about the place in the poem. The little book becomes the beginning of a much longer conversation.
Nobody else is in the classroom. Only Mia is here.
The organiser counts more than nine thousand visitors at an exhibition. People fill several large halls, and many more are still waiting outside.
In a space story, an engineer cheers after a launch. The craft is now following a path around the Earth and repeats the journey without landing.

Before our art club leaves school, the leader checks a list of everyone's names. We carry paper and pencils up a hill outside the town. The landscape below includes a river, green fields and many small houses. Some pupils draw the river while others choose the shapes of the houses. When I cannot find my eraser, a friend lets me use hers. Before the bus leaves, our leader checks the names again to make sure nobody is missing. Everyone returns with a different picture of the same place.

During a museum visit, our guide shows a model of our town's historic bridge. It first connected the two river banks and changed local life, she explains. At first, I notice only the shape of the model. The guide gives us a tip: look at the old map before studying the newer one. The old map shows separate villages, but the newer one shows roads joining them. Now I understand why people remember this bridge, not just how it looks. I add a note about the maps beside my drawing.
Yesterday, two towns opened the first bridge between them. After years of separation, people can meet easily, and the opening will be remembered in their history.
A pupil often puts the wrong label on a cup during a science task. Her partner suggests writing the labels before filling the cups so they will not be confused.

Our street club holds a friendly chess afternoon for neighbours. Mr Wu, a senior, offers to play the first game with me. My aunt is an adult who volunteers to keep the scores for the tables. I try to win quickly and move a piece without looking carefully. Mr Wu asks me to look at all the pieces before my next move. This time I wait, think and find a better place for my piece. I do not win, but I leave wanting to play another game.

A notice outside our park announces a new library. My friend worries that the town will remove our favourite garden to build it. We read the small map and find that the library site is across the street from the park. It is an empty yard, not the garden inside the park. The poster also shows a path from the park gate to the future library entrance. My friend smiles because we will keep the garden and gain a place to read. Before telling others, we check the map once more.
The door opens and Lin sees the puppy she missed all week. Her face immediately brightens, and she smiles before the puppy even reaches her.
A family follows a path to a pool formed by rain and rocks. Nobody built the pool; it is part of the wild hillside.
I have a happy memory of our family picnic.
我对那次家庭野餐有一段愉快的回忆。
My brother has a good memory for names.
我的哥哥／弟弟很善于记住名字。
In the film, the general leads the army across the river.
电影中，将军率领军队过河。
She smiles at the sight of her old friend.
This path leads to a natural lake.
这条小路通向一个天然湖泊。
The sky becomes dark in the evening.

During my first week at junior high school, I struggle to choose an activity. After sitting in lessons, I am still full of energy and want to move. Older pupils invite me to try table tennis during the lunch break. I cannot control the ball well, so one pupil shows me a slower practice. We pass the ball gently across the table instead of playing a match. By Friday, I can keep the ball moving for several turns. I put the club time on my timetable and look forward to the next week.

My brother is good at cooking, but I know only how to make toast. On Saturday, I ask him to teach me one easy meal. He chooses vegetable rice and lets me wash the vegetables while he cuts them. While the rice cooks, he explains each step and answers my questions. After we eat, I offer to do the dishes to thank him for teaching me. He wipes the table, and together we leave the kitchen tidy. I write the steps in a notebook so I can try the meal again.
The weather can influence our plans for a picnic.
Mia makes a small clay bird and displays it with drawings made by her classmates. Visitors look at these creative objects at the school show.
Ben dips a brush in coloured paint and moves it over paper. He learns how to use light and dark colours in his pictures.
The town is a gateway to the mountains.
这个镇是通往山区的门户。
The weather can influence our plans.
天气会影响我们的计划。
Students show their artwork in the school hall.
学生们在学校大厅展示他们的艺术作品。
Mia enjoys painting with bright colours.
米娅喜欢用明亮的色彩绘画。
The picture shows a busy market scene.
这幅画展示了一个热闹的市场场景。
Mr Li and his wife visit the museum together.
李先生和他的妻子一起参观博物馆。

An empty room beside our library has almost no chairs or shelves. Our class wants it to become a reading space for younger pupils. Each family offers one useful thing, such as a cushion or a small table. We draw a plan before placing anything, leaving a clear path to the door. Mia labels the book boxes while Ben checks where the lamps can stand. When everything is in place, the younger pupils choose books and try the new seats. The room changes because many people share a small amount of work.

Our teacher brings leaves and small stones to the art room. She asks us to draw their natural shapes instead of making every line perfect. At the sight of a leaf with an uneven edge, Ben begins to notice tiny details. He sees that one side is wider and that several holes let light through. Mia chooses a stone and uses several colours to show its marks. We compare the drawings and see that close looking matters more than matching a perfect shape.
Visitors come from far away to see the old garden. The town map marks it as a place to visit during a holiday.
At dusk, the worker switches on lamps along the path. The dark path becomes bright enough for people to see.
The old bridge is made of stone.
Ben picks up a smooth stone beside the river.
本在河边捡起一块光滑的石头。
I can see my reflection in the mirror.
我能在镜子里看见自己的映像。
The old bridge is a popular tourist spot.
这座老桥是一个受欢迎的旅游景点。
Small lamps light up the garden at night.
A small garden is in the centre of the square.
一个小花园位于广场中央。
Mia is interested in space and reads books about the moon.
米娅对太空有兴趣，会阅读有关月球的书。

Mr Chen and his wife make breakfast at their small shop every morning. Their daughter takes a photograph of the busy scene for her school project. In the photograph, one person cooks while the other speaks to waiting customers. The daughter asks permission before including anyone's face in her display. She also writes short notes about the different jobs her parents share. Her classmates enjoy learning how one ordinary family works together to begin the day.

Our museum has a small room where children can try painting. Mia uses a brush and two colours to show a rainy street. She leaves some white space so the lights seem to shine on the wet road. Her artwork is only one of many different things in the room. There are clay animals, paper flowers and drawings by younger visitors too. Before leaving, everyone shares one idea about how they made their work. The room shows us that people can express ideas in more than one way.
The town plants a tree in memory of a teacher who helped many children.
The club reads poems, stories and plays from different writers. Members talk about the ideas and language in these works.
Mia wears a costume on stage and speaks the lines of a grandmother in a play. She is not speaking as herself.
The old city wall is a historic site.
这段古城墙是一处历史遗迹。
The town builds a small garden in memory of a brave doctor.
镇上修建了一个小花园，以纪念一位勇敢的医生。
Stories and poems are forms of literature.
故事和诗歌是文学的不同形式。
扮演（戏剧、电影中的角色）
Ben acts as a king in the school play.
本在学校戏剧中扮演国王。
We take time to appreciate the beauty of the garden.
我们花时间欣赏花园的美。
The teacher appreciates Mia's careful work.
老师赏识米娅认真的工作。
I want to join the school art club.
我想加入学校美术社团。
Ben joins our game after lunch.
本午饭后加入我们的游戏。

A small garden stands in the centre of our town, with streets on every side. Mia is interested in the plants there and wants to learn their names. She asks the gardener whether the reading club can help make simple labels. The gardener agrees and checks each name before the pupils write it neatly. Ben adds small drawings so visitors can match the labels to the plants. The project turns Mia's curiosity into something useful for everyone who visits.

The old bridge is a tourist spot that many families visit at weekends. Our town puts small lamps beside the path to light up the bridge after dark. Mia visits with her grandfather and compares the evening view with a daytime photograph. The shape is the same, but the lamps make the stone lines easier to see. Grandfather points out a seat where they can rest without blocking the path. They sit and draw the bridge before walking home together. Mia discovers that returning to a familiar place at a new time can change what she notices.
We buy fruit and handmade toys at the village fair.
The tall vehicle has a pointed top and powerful engines. It carries a satellite up from the ground and into space.
A team counts down as a spacecraft waits on the ground. At zero, they send it upwards to begin its journey into space.
I will definitely come to your birthday party.
我肯定会来参加你的生日聚会。
We buy handmade toys at the village fair.
我们在乡村集市买手工玩具。
The rocket rises into the sky.
The team launches a small rocket into the sky.
团队把一枚小火箭发射升空。
The children shout with excitement when their team scores.
队伍得分时，孩子们兴奋地大叫。
The wind gives the small boat power to move.
风为这条小船提供前进的动力。
The toy car gets power from a battery.
玩具车从电池中获取能量。

Ella wants to join the music club, but she knows little about playing with a group. The members invite her to listen before choosing an instrument. At first, she notices only the loud drum at the front. Then she learns to appreciate the careful work of the quieter players too. A soft tune from the back helps connect the different parts of the song. Ella asks to practise that part, and another member sits beside her to help. Listening first gives her a better understanding of how the whole group works.

Our reading group chooses a short story from a book of literature. It tells of a young gardener who asks an older neighbour for help. We decide to show one part of the story as a short play. I act the part of the gardener, while Mia plays the neighbour. Before speaking our lines, we discuss why each character makes a different choice. The performance helps us notice ideas that we miss when we read quickly. Afterwards, everyone returns to the book with new questions about the characters.
“Can you help us carry the books?” “Definitely! I am happy to help.”
Mrs Green is married to Mr Green. They share a home, and their daughter calls both of them her parents.
A photograph shows customers waiting while shopkeepers serve breakfast. Several people are talking and carrying trays at the same time.

The science club brings a toy car to the school open day. A small battery gives the motor power to turn the wheels. Before each test, the visitors count to three and shout, “Go!” together. Ben marks the stopping place with a card so everyone can compare the runs. Mia explains that they change only one thing at a time, such as the wheels. The younger children enjoy guessing the car's stopping place and checking their ideas. The demonstration gives everyone a chance to ask questions instead of only watching.

At the space museum, our class watches a film about a rocket. The vehicle stands on the ground while a team checks its equipment. They test the instruments before they launch it into the sky. The film shows that many people have different jobs before the journey begins. After watching, we put picture cards in the order shown on the screen. Mia adds notes about checking, waiting and finally leaving the ground. Our display focuses on preparation, not just the exciting moment at the end.
The spacecraft is ready on the ground. After the final checks, the team sends it upwards to start its flight.
In the museum film, a tall vehicle rises on a strong jet from its engines. It carries equipment away from Earth into space.

Our history group visits a historic site with stone steps and an old gate. A guide asks us to look carefully before taking out our notebooks. Mia begins to appreciate the careful work in the small stone patterns. Ben notices worn steps and imagines the many visitors who use them. We sketch the details from the public path without touching or moving anything. Later, we compare our notes and find that each person notices a different detail. The visit teaches us to spend time looking at old places instead of only collecting photographs.

The library invites our class to share a story from a book of literature. The story has two children who disagree about the way to a garden. Mia and I act the parts of the children while another pupil reads the setting. We use different voices to show that one character is worried and the other is confident. After the reading, younger visitors ask why the characters do not check a map together. Their questions help us see a possible solution that neither character tries. Sharing the story becomes a discussion, with the listeners adding ideas of their own.
Lily traces around a leaf on paper. The line shows its outline, with a wide middle and a pointed end.
A group wears walking boots and follows a long path through the hills. They travel on foot for several hours, enjoying the countryside.
Please wait a moment while I find my keys.
请稍等片刻，我找一下钥匙。
Mia is a member of the school music club.
米娅是学校音乐社团的一名成员。
This box has the shape of a star.
这个盒子的形状像星星。
We hike through the hills on Sunday.
星期日我们在山间徒步旅行。
A new bookshop opened near our school recently.
最近，一家新书店在我们学校附近开业了。
Parents attend the school meeting on Friday.
家长们星期五参加学校会议。

Our class wants to take a trip to the hills during the school holiday. There are two paths from the bus stop, one steep and one more gentle. We decide to use the gentle path because some pupils are carrying heavy drawing equipment. The teacher gives everyone time to rest and check their bags before leaving. On the way, we stop beside a field and make quick drawings. The longer but easier route lets the whole group enjoy the visit together. We learn that choosing a route means thinking about everyone, not only the fastest walker.

Our radio club needs a quiet place to record an interview. At first, we choose a seat beside the main road in the town. The sound of buses is the reason we cannot hear the speaker clearly. Mia suggests a quieter part of the town near a small garden. We try recording one question there and listen to it before beginning again. The new recording is easier to understand, so we continue in the garden. A short test helps us choose a better place before spending time on the whole interview.
These handmade bags are for sale, not for borrowing.
It is the short break between lunch and dinner. Ben eats a small amount of fruit and a biscuit, not a full meal.
The pupils hang paper flowers and colourful pictures around the plain room. They want it to look cheerful for the visitors.
This charity helps children buy school books.
这个慈善机构帮助孩子们购买课本。
The shop has books for sale.
I eat a small snack after school.
We decorate the classroom with paper flowers.
The main difference between the bags is their size.
这两个袋子的主要差别是大小。
Students from six schools compete in the race.
来自六所学校的学生参加这场比赛。

Recently, our class went to a meeting about the new community centre. Parents and children attended together so everyone could suggest useful activities. Mia asked for a quiet reading corner with a low shelf for younger children. Ben suggested a table where pupils could share drawings and craft ideas. A worker wrote each idea on a board and checked that the children agreed with her notes. Before leaving, we each received a copy to discuss back at school. The meeting showed us that children can explain their needs and listen to other people too.

Our walking group likes to hike along the marked path above the lake. Today, the teacher asks us to draw landmarks that help us remember the route. Ben draws a rock with a pointed shape, like a large triangle. Mia chooses the curved edge of the lake because it looks like the letter C. We add labels and compare the drawings with the path on our map. On the return walk, the landmarks help us recognise where to stop and rest. Our pictures become useful notes rather than just souvenirs of a pleasant walk.
Mia's school holds a fair every October. It happens once each year, and families mark the date on their calendars.
Ben watches the show and claps for a long time. He says it is wonderful and praises the music, colours and costumes.
The school concert is a popular event for families.
学校音乐会是深受家庭欢迎的一项活动。
I eat the soup with a spoon.
The annual school fair takes place every October.
学校一年一度的展会在每年十月举行。
The class gives a fantastic performance.
全班带来了一场极好的表演。
元（美国、加拿大、澳大利亚等国的货币单位）
这个笔记本的价格是一元。
Dad makes an apple pie for dessert.
爸爸做了一个苹果派作为甜点。

Our school has two races that pupils can choose to compete in. The main difference is that one is for individuals and the other is a team relay. In the relay, each runner carries a baton and passes it to the next person. Mia chooses the relay because she enjoys practising with friends. The team learns to wait in the right place and make each pass clear. On race day, classmates cheer for every runner, not only the first one to finish. Both races give pupils a chance to try, but the relay also asks them to work together.

Our class prepares a welcome table for pupils who are new to the school. We decorate it with paper flowers and pictures of different school activities. Mia writes a short list showing where visitors can ask for help. After the school tour, each new pupil has a small snack of fruit during the break. Older pupils sit nearby and answer questions about clubs and lessons. One visitor says that talking over food makes it easier to ask a question. The table helps turn a strange new place into somewhere with familiar faces.
School clubs introduce themselves and invite new members at the clubs fair.
Sunlight falls on panels on a roof. The panels use that sunlight to produce electricity for the building.
Mia asks, “May I join your game?” Lily smiles and says, “Yes, you are very welcome. There is room for you.”
The club keeps its sports equipment in this room.
社团把体育器材存放在这个房间。
We meet the science club at the clubs fair.
我们在社团招募展上了解科学社团。
These lights use solar power from the Sun.
这些灯使用来自太阳的太阳能。
Of course you can join us. There is room for one more.
你当然可以加入我们。还有一个位置。
Use the remote control to turn on the television.
Please turn around and look at the board behind you.
请转身，看看你身后的黑板。

My cousin in Canada helps her class run a stall at the school fair. They sell slices of apple pie, with sweet fruit inside a baked pastry case. Each slice costs one dollar, and the price is written clearly beside the tray. Mia serves the slices while Ben puts each payment into a box. Another pupil records every sale so they can check the money afterwards. They work in short turns so everyone has time to see the other stalls. Sharing clear jobs helps the children serve visitors and keep track of their class project.

Our annual science show takes place once every year in the school hall. Each group prepares a model and explains one question it wants to investigate. This year, our group shows how different paper wings change a model plane's flight. Visitors try two versions and tell us what they notice. One younger pupil calls the show fantastic because she can ask questions and test ideas herself. Her questions give us a new idea to try after the show. The display for this year ends, but we still have more ideas to explore.
Young children attend primary school before they go to secondary school.
An apple is hanging from a branch. A strong wind shakes the branch, and the apple drops to the ground.
Mia cuts a circle from thick paper and removes a smaller circle from its middle. The piece now has a hole in the centre.
Small acts of kindness can make a difference.
小小的善举也能发挥作用。
My little sister goes to primary school.
Leaves fall off the tree in autumn.
The children stand in a ring.
孩子们围成一个圆圈站着。
Mia shows us her collection of coins.
米娅给我们看她的硬币收藏。
My aunt owns a small shop.
我的阿姨拥有一家小店。

The technology club tests a small toy car in the school hall. Nora holds the remote control and checks which buttons make the car move. Her partner stands behind her and asks her to turn around before he explains the route. They agree to keep the car away from the chairs so that there is enough space. On the first try, Nora presses the wrong button, so they stop and look at the labels together. After a second careful try, the car follows the route, and the partners record which buttons they used.

Our class takes a small lamp on a daytime trip to the school garden. The lamp uses solar power, so we put its panel where it can receive sunlight. Leo asks the teacher whether he may help choose the place for it. “Of course,” she says, and asks him to explain why one place is better than another. He notices that a tree shades one corner, so he chooses an open spot instead. The pupils draw both places in their notebooks and write why the open spot is better for the lamp.
The children join hands and stand in a ring.
Several school teams enter the same race. Each team tries to finish first under the same rules.
Two pictures look nearly the same. In one picture the door is blue, but in the other it is green.

Some older pupils return to their primary school to help with an art afternoon. They bring paper leaves to hang from a small display tree near the classroom door. When the door opens, a few leaves fall off because their string loops are too loose. The pupils stop hanging new leaves and check the loops that are already on the tree. They fix the loose ones and invite the younger children to add their drawings. By the end of the afternoon, the display shows work from both groups of pupils.

A group of friends wants to help keep the reading room quiet and tidy. They do not own the room or the books, so they first ask the librarian what help is useful. She suggests returning books to the right places and speaking softly near readers. The friends follow her advice for a week instead of changing things without asking. Their small actions make a difference: readers can find books more easily and work with fewer interruptions. The friends decide to keep helping, with the librarian’s guidance.
There are two primary schools for younger children in our town.
A pupil moves a heavy box away from a narrow doorway. Now everyone can pass through the doorway easily.
This bicycle belongs to Sara. She bought it with money she saved, and nobody else is its owner.

The technology club plans a model house for the school fair. Its roof has a small panel that uses solar power to run a tiny fan in sunlight. One member asks whether visitors may move the model closer to the window. “Of course, if we move it carefully together,” says the club leader. They mark a clear place on the table so that the panel will not be shaded by another model. Their explanation card tells visitors what supplies the energy and why the position matters.

At the clubs fair, pupils visit different tables to learn what each group does. The photography club shows its equipment, including a camera, a stand and a small lamp. Members let visitors look closely before explaining which items may be tried with help. Hana likes taking pictures but needs help with the camera stand, so she asks for a demonstration. She learns how it keeps the camera still and writes down the club’s meeting time. She plans to ask more questions before choosing a club, rather than joining only because a table looks exciting.
Ben pulls on a hand covering before working. The covering has a separate part for each of his fingers.
The mixture needs more water. Mia puts one more spoonful into the bowl and stirs it.
This old coin is valuable and costs a lot of money.
这枚古硬币很贵重，值很多钱。
Please do not handle the glass objects without gloves.
不戴手套请不要用手触摸这些玻璃制品。
I wear gloves to keep my hands warm.
Please add some water to the soup.
Put the letter in an envelope.
The view from the hill is absolutely fantastic.
从山丘上看到的风景极其美妙。

Our geography group prepares a fact file about the trees in the school garden. Each page records an observed detail, such as where a tree stands and what its leaves look like. We take the pages outside to check that our descriptions match the actual trees. A sudden wind begins to blow away the loose pages, so we quickly hold them down. We put the pages on a firm board with a clip before continuing our checks. Back in class, we correct two descriptions and keep the final file together in a folder.

Our science club makes a wall display about the solar system. We draw the Sun and the planets on separate cards so that we can arrange the model carefully. One member wants to fill the background with hundreds of tiny paper stars. Before we begin, the teacher asks whether a crowded background will make the main labels harder to read. We try a small section first, then choose fewer stars and larger labels. The finished display is easier to follow because the main information does not get lost among the decorations.
There is just one ticket left for the show. No second ticket is available.
A carpenter uses a hammer to push a small pointed metal pin into wood. The pin holds two pieces together.
This bag seems heavy. Can I help you carry it?
这个包好像很重。我能帮你拿吗？
It is impossible for a person to live without water.
人不喝水是无法活下去的。
There is a single coin in the box.
The worker hits a nail into the wood.
工人把一枚钉子敲进木头。
The teacher explains the rule with an example.
老师用一个例子说明规则。
There is a small bit of bread on the plate.
